solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Victor, struggling with pesky rent, being this?

definitions.text: Victor, struggling with pesky rent, being this?

indicators.note: the letters of victor and pesky rent are struggling, thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Victor wrestles with a troublesome rent bill and wonders whether he is now penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor is here the whole word, not the V of the phonetic alphabet; all fifteen letters of VICTOR and PESKY RENT are rearranged, and the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone struggling to pay an irksome rent might well be destitute, which is what the phrase describes.

clue.text: One having turned up barman at first tolerated?

definitions.text: One having turned up barman at first tolerated?

indicators.note: turned means the word up is read the other way round
at first means only the opening letter of barman is used

parts.note: first letter of barman
to bore someone is to have them put up with you, so tolerated stands for the past tense, bore

explanation.surface: A tiresome regular arrives at the bar, and the barman has no choice but to put up with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses UP to give PU; add B from barman and BORE. The whole clue describes such a person: they turn up and the barman puts up with them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedious drinker who corners others with dull talk in a bar is the classic figure of the phrase.

clue.text: Engine's sound and very secure on ascent

indicators.note: in a down clue, on ascent means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to moor a boat is to secure it

explanation.surface: A mechanic praises an engine's noise and how firmly it is fixed when climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the imitative word for the roar of a revving motor, so it names the noise an engine makes.

clue.text: For auditors, generate an invoice in the form of a flyer

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so for auditors means the phrase is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: to generate an invoice is to raise a bill

explanation.surface: Accountants are asked to issue an invoice designed to look like a leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' pretends to be a printed leaflet, fitting the invoice picture, but it is a bird. 'auditors' looks like accountants; here it means listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: The razorbill is a black-and-white seabird of the auk family, and any bird is a flyer.

clue.text: What can appear long until just before November?

definitions.text: What can appear long until just before November?

indicators.note: until just before means the word stops short of the letter for November, so that letter is lost

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn
N is November in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what can seem to drag on all the way to the eleventh month.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a twelve-month span can feel long, especially by late autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A twelve-month calendar span can feel drawn-out, especially by the time autumn comes round.

clue.text: Chinese city's restriction on books leading to offence

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a tie is something that restricts or binds
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible
a sin is an offence against moral law

explanation.surface: A Chinese city's ban on certain books ends up causing offence.
explanation.walkthrough: TIENTSIN is the older Western spelling of Tianjin, a port city in northern China.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the older Western romanisation of Tianjin, a major port and municipality in northern China.

clue.text: One judge is up in arms

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
to rate something is to judge or assess it

explanation.surface: A single judge is furious about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up in arms is an idiom for being angry and protesting, which matches being furious.

clue.text: A bargain in pink and blue

parts.note: an engine pinks or knocks when its fuel ignites too early, making a metallic rattle
feeling blue means feeling down

explanation.surface: A cheap item for sale comes in pink and blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pink' and 'blue' look like colours; one is an engine's rattle and the other a low mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockdown price is one slashed very low, so the word describes a cheap deal.

clue.text: Few like such garments merely to be the first for wearing?

definitions.text: Few like such garments merely to be the first for wearing?

parts.words: Few like such garments merely to be the first for wearing?
parts.note: the clue asks what to do to the word few: treat it like a shirt that needs no pressing, take away the chemical symbol for that metal, and only W is left

explanation.surface: Seemingly a remark that few people enjoy clothes that are only good for the first time they are worn.
explanation.walkthrough: FE is the chemical symbol for iron. Take FE out of FEW and only W remains, the first letter of wearing. So the answer describes what has happened to the word Few.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments that need no pressing after washing are labelled this way; here the label is applied to the word few, which loses its Fe.

clue.text: Boast about French XI, first in Europe for a time

indicators.note: about means brag goes around the French word for eleven

parts.note: to brag is to boast
XI is eleven, which in French is onze

indicators.note: first in means only the opening letter of Europe is used

parts.note: first letter of Europe

explanation.surface: Bragging about a French football team that was the first in Europe for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'XI' looks like a team of eleven players; here it is just the number, put into French.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bronze Age is a prehistoric period when copper alloys were the main material for tools, so it names an era.

clue.text: A party with sailors on deck

parts.note: a do is a party
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: A party held with the crew up on the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like part of a ship, fitting the sailors, but it is the verb to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something, as in decking the halls, is to decorate it, which is what the answer means.

clue.text: Seafood requisitions taking months, not days

indicators.note: taking means the word for requisitions gains the letter for months
not means the letter for days is dropped where months goes in

parts.note: requisitions are formal orders

explanation.surface: Orders for seafood that take months rather than days to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormers are edible abalone shellfish found around the Channel Islands, so they are a kind of seafood.

clue.text: Better without clothing for race, one would agree?

definitions.text: Better without clothing for race, one would agree?

indicators.note: without in the sense of outside: the word for better goes round the other letters

parts.note: one who bets is a better, or staker

indicators.note: the clothing of a word is its outer letters, so this takes the first and last letters of race

explanation.surface: Someone argues that a race is better run naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like the comparative of good; it is a person who bets. The whole clue also describes the answer: one who runs across a sports field naked.
explanation.definitionFit: A streaker dashes naked across a public place, so would agree that running unclothed is best.

clue.text: Need large one before retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back to bed, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room; the setter's parse needs its middle two letters swapped

explanation.surface: A demand for one large drink before going to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue is flawed: 'retiring' reverses L, I and ANTE to give ETNAIL, not the answer. The setter needed ENTA backwards, and the online version was corrected to an anagram of L, I and NEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to require it as a necessary consequence, so the verb works as a synonym of need.

clue.text: Pour tea to start: I must have mine to drink!

indicators.note: to start means only the opening letter of tea is used

parts.note: first letter of tea
a pit is a coal mine
to down a drink is to swallow it in one go

explanation.surface: Someone demanding to pour the tea first and insisting their own cup gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pour' looks like serving tea, but it means rain hard; to tip it down is British slang for heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, when it is tipping it down the rain is falling very heavily, as in pouring with rain.

clue.text: Overused, of dubious merit now

indicators.note: dubious letters are doubtful and unsettled, so the letters of merit now get reordered

explanation.surface: Something tired and overdone, whose worth is now questionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timeworn is worn out by long use, as in a timeworn cliché, so it means hackneyed.

clue.text: Match involving four old clubs is undecided

indicators.note: involving means equal takes the other letters inside itself

parts.note: to match something is to equal it
IV is four in Roman numerals
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A game involving four veteran golf clubs ends with no clear result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests a sports team or golf; it is just the card suit letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: An equivocal answer is ambiguous and leaves things open, so the word describes something not settled.

clue.text: One coming before performances to record shows

indicators.note: shows means the answer is on display inside the words performances to record

explanation.surface: An opening act whose performances are to be recorded and broadcast as shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' looks like a noun about performances, but it is the verb, displaying letters in plain view.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear comes earlier in the family line, so an ancestor is one who came before you.

clue.text: Replace spades, having finished with machinery

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades
when time is up it is finished
plant means industrial machinery and equipment

explanation.surface: A gardener swaps out the spades once they have finished with the machines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spades' looks like garden tools, fitting the machinery; it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplant someone is to take their place or oust them, so it means to substitute for.

clue.text: Jump in fare after auction ends early

indicators.note: after means the food comes behind the shortened sale
ends early means the word stops before its last letter, so that final letter is lost

parts.note: an auction is a sale
chow is slang for food, or fare

explanation.surface: Prices for fares leap once an auction finishes ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: A salchow is a figure-skating jump, named after the Swedish skater Ulrich Salchow.
explanation.definitionFit: The salchow is a figure-skating leap in which the skater takes off from the back inside edge.

clue.text: A cuff you weren't expecting?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the folded-up hem at the bottom of a trouser leg

explanation.surface: A slap on the ear that catches you by surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuff' looks like a blow; it is the turned-back hem of trousers. 'A turn-up for the books' is British for an unexpected event.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a folded trouser hem and, in British idiom, a surprising development.

clue.text: They'd ruin sea trip?

indicators.note: to ruin the words sea trip is to wreck their order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about who would spoil a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: buccaneers boarding a ship would spoil any cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea robbers who board and plunder ships would certainly wreck a voyage for those aboard.

clue.text: I get browned off, swamped by stories and dull speeches

indicators.note: swamped by means the I and the tan are surrounded by the word for stories

parts.note: lies are stories in the sense of untruths
to tan is to get browned by the sun, here in the sense of browned off by sunbathing

explanation.surface: Someone fed up by tall tales and tedious addresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'browned off' is British slang for fed up, which the surface uses; in the wordplay it just means sunburnt.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a long tedious recital or list, so the plural fits wearisome speeches.

clue.text: Be able to broadcast under any conditions?

indicators.note: broadcast means the phrase is heard aloud rather than read

parts.note: to have the know-how is to be able to do something

explanation.surface: A question about whether one can transmit in all circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: Nohow is a dialect word for 'in no way'; the question mark admits the definition is the negative, as in 'not under any conditions'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nohow is a dialect word meaning not in any way, which is the negative sense of the phrase given.

clue.text: Image from bible with A-rating

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
a rating is an ordinary sailor, as is a tar

explanation.surface: A picture drawn from the scriptures that has earned top marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A-rating' looks like a grade; split it into A and rating, a naval word for a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is a figure representing a person, online or as a god's incarnation, so it is a kind of icon.

clue.text: Sequence to work out

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to exercise or practise, as athletes do

explanation.walkthrough: 'work out' looks like solving something; it means to exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a connected series of events and a verb for exercising to get fit.

clue.text: French day centre's abandoned by Order of the Republic?

indicators.note: the centre of the French word, its middle letter, is abandoned or left out

parts.note: jeudi is French for Thursday

explanation.surface: On a French holiday a day centre is closed by government decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order of the Republic' sounds like a French honour; it is the Jedi Order of Star Wars, which served the Galactic Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: In Star Wars the Jedi are a knightly order who protect the Galactic Republic, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Spirit primarily cordial in houses backing onto one another

indicators.note: in means that letter goes inside the pair of houses

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house; two of them, the second turned round so their backs meet

indicators.note: primarily means only the opening letter of cordial is used

parts.note: first letter of cordial

explanation.surface: A neighbourly drink first poured in terraced houses built back to back.
explanation.walkthrough: HO is the abbreviation for house: one written forwards and one backwards gives HO OH, back to back, with C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooch is slang for strong alcohol, especially cheap or illicit liquor, so it is a type of spirit.

clue.text: Sharp right turns in front of entrance

indicators.note: in front of means the turned letters come first
turns means the abbreviation for right is turned round

parts.note: to entrance, stressed on the second syllable, is to enchant

explanation.surface: A sharp right-hand turn just before the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like a doorway, but it is the verb meaning to captivate.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant criticism is incisive and cutting, so the word means keen or biting.

clue.text: Where St Vincent, seeing snake, protected people, keeping lives secure

parts.note: to snake is to wind, as a road winds

indicators.note: keeping means the wards hold the other letters inside them

parts.note: wards are people placed under someone's protection
is in the sense of exists or lives
to land a deal or a fish is to secure it

explanation.surface: A saint sees a snake and keeps those in his care safe.
explanation.walkthrough: St Vincent is not a saint here but a Caribbean island; 'seeing' is a link word. The Windward Islands are the southern Lesser Antilles.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Vincent belongs to the Windward Islands, a Caribbean chain in the southern Lesser Antilles.
